paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: Suppose your university is seeking students’ opinions on whether university canteens should be open to the public. You are now to write an essay to express your view. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：假设您的大学正在征求学生关于大学食堂是否应向公众开放的意见。你现在要写一篇文章来表达你的观点。您将有 30 分钟的时间来完成该任务。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear three news reports. At the end of each news report, you will hear two or three questions. Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A), B), C) and D). Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明： 在本节中，您将听到三则新闻报道。在每篇新闻报道的最后，你都会听到两到三个问题。新闻报道和提问均只发言一次。听到问题后，您必须从标有 A)、B)、C) 和 D) 的四个选项中选择最佳答案。然后在答卷 1 上用一条穿过中心的线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.translationZh: 问题1和2是根据你刚才听到的新闻报道得出的。

You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s well known that physical exercise is beneficial not just to physical health but also to mental health. Yet whereas most countries have 26 , evidence-backed guidelines on the type and intensity of exercise 27 for various physical health benefits, such guidelines do not yet exist for exercise and mood. This is 28 due to a lack of necessary evidence. However, a new systematic review brings us usefully up-to-date on the current findings in this area.
paragraphs.translationZh: 众所周知，体育锻炼不仅有益于身体健康，也有益于心理健康。然而，尽管大多数国家针对各种身体健康益处所需的运动类型和强度制定了详细的、有证据支持的指南，但针对运动和情绪的指南尚不存在。部分原因是缺乏必要的证据。然而，一项新的系统回顾为我们提供了该领域当前研究结果的有用信息。

paragraphs.sourceText: Before 29 into some of the key take-aways, an important 30 made in the review is between aerobic exercise and anaerobic. The former 31 such things as walking, jogging and cycling and means exercising in such a way that your body is able to use oxygen to burn fat for energy. In contrast, anaerobic exercise — such as lifting heavy weights — is of such 32 intensity that your body does not have time to use oxygen to create energy and so instead it breaks down glucose (葡萄糖) in your blood or muscles.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在深入探讨一些关键要点之前，回顾中的一个重要区别是有氧运动和无氧运动。前者涉及步行、慢跑和骑自行车等活动，意味着您的身体能够利用氧气燃烧脂肪来获取能量。相比之下，无氧运动（例如举重）的强度非常大，以至于您的身体没有时间利用氧气来产生能量，因此它会分解血液或肌肉中的葡萄糖。

paragraphs.sourceText: Beginning first with the influence of exercise intensity on the mood benefits of aerobic exercise, the researchers, led by John Chan at Shenzhen University, found 33 results from 19 relevant studies. Some favoured higher intensity, others low, while seven studies found that intensity made no 34 to mood benefits.
paragraphs.translationZh: 深圳大学 John Chan 领导的研究人员首先从运动强度对有氧运动的情绪益处的影响入手，发现 19 项相关研究结果相互矛盾。有些人喜欢较高的强度，有些人喜欢较低的强度，而七项研究发现强度对情绪的好处没有影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: In relation to the intensity of anaerobic exercise, however, the results were far clearer — the optimum (最佳选择) for improving mood is 35 intensity, perhaps because low intensity is too dull while high intensity is too unpleasant.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，就无氧运动的强度而言，结果要清楚得多——改善情绪的最佳选择是中等强度，也许是因为低强度太沉闷，而高强度太不愉快。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Why Do Americans Work So Much?
paragraphs.translationZh: 为什么美国人工作这么多？

paragraphs.sourceText: A) How will we all keep busy when we only have to work 15 hours a week? That was the question that worried the British economist John Maynard Keynes when he wrote his short essay “Economic Possibilities for Our Grandchildren” in 1930. Over the next century, he predicted, the economy would become so productive that people would barely need to work at all. For a while, it looked like Keynes was right. In 1930 the average working week was 47 hours in the United States. But by 1970, the number of hours Americans worked on average had fallen to slightly less than 39.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 当我们每周只需工作 15 小时时，我们如何保持忙碌？这是英国经济学家约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯 (John Maynard Keynes) 在 1930 年撰写短文《我们子孙的经济可能性》时所担心的问题。他预测，在下个世纪，经济将变得如此富有成效，以至于人们几乎不需要工作。有一段时间，凯恩斯似乎是对的。 1930 年，美国每周平均工作时间为 47 小时。但到 1970 年，美国人的平均工作时间已降至略低于 39 小时。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) But then something changed. Instead of continuing to decline, the duration of the working week remained stable. It has stayed at just below 40 hours for nearly five decades. So what happened? Why are people working just as much today as in 1970?
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 但后来事情发生了变化。每周工作时间并没有继续下降，而是保持稳定。近 50 年来，它一直保持在 40 小时以下。那么发生了什么？为什么今天人们的工作量和 1970 年一样多？

paragraphs.sourceText: C) There would be no mystery in this if Keynes had been wrong about the power of technology to increase the economy’s productivity, which he thought would lead to a standard of living “between four and eight times as high as it is today.” But Keynes got that right: Technology has made the economy massively more productive. According to Benjamin M. Friedman, an economist at Harvard, the U.S. economy is right on track to reach Keynes’s eight-fold (八倍) multiple by 2029. That is a century after the last data Keynes would have had access to.
paragraphs.translationZh: C）如果凯恩斯关于技术提高经济生产力的力量的看法是错误的，那么这就不是什么神秘的事情了，他认为这将导致生活水平“比今天高四到八倍”。但凯恩斯说得对：技术极大地提高了经济的生产力。哈佛大学经济学家本杰明·M·弗里德曼 (Benjamin M. Friedman) 表示，美国经济有望在 2029 年达到凯恩斯的八倍 (八倍)。距凯恩斯上次获得数据已经一个世纪了。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) In a new paper, Friedman tries to figure out why that increased productivity has not translated into increased leisure time. Perhaps people just never feel materially satisfied, always wanting more money to buy the next new thing. This is a theory that appeals to many economists. “This argument is, at best, far from sufficient,” he writes. If that were the case, why did the duration of the working week decline in the first place?
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 在一篇新论文中，弗里德曼试图找出为什么生产力的提高没有转化为休闲时间的增加。也许人们只是永远不会在物质上感到满足，总是想要更多的钱来购买下一个新事物。这是一个吸引许多经济学家的理论。 “这个论点充其量是远远不够的，”他写道。如果是这样的话，为什么每周的工作时间会减少呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Another theory Friedman considers is that, in an era of ever fewer settings that provide effective opportunities for personal connections and relationships, people may place more value on the socializing that happens at work. There is support for this theory. Many people today consider colleagues as friends. But Friedman argues that the evidence for this theory is far from conclusive. Many workers report that they would like to spend more time with family, rather than at work. Furthermore, this theory cannot explain the change in trend in the U.S. working week in the 1970s.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 弗里德曼认为的另一个理论是，在一个为个人联系和人际关系提供有效机会的环境越来越少的时代，人们可能会更重视工作中发生的社交活动。这个理论是有支持的。如今，许多人将同事视为朋友。但弗里德曼认为，这一理论的证据远非结论性的。许多员工表示，他们希望花更多时间陪伴家人，而不是工作。此外，这一理论无法解释 20 世纪 70 年代美国工作周趋势的变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) A third possibility proves more convincing for Friedman. That is: American inequality means that the gains of increasing productivity are not widely shared by everyone. In other words, most Americans are too poor to work less. Unlike the other two explanations Friedman considers, this one fits chronologically (按年代). Inequality declined in America during the period following World War II, along with the duration of the working week. But since the early 1970s it has risen dramatically.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 第三种可能性对弗里德曼来说更有说服力。也就是说：美国的不平等意味着生产力提高的收益并未被所有人广泛分享。换句话说，大多数美国人太穷了，无法减少工作。与弗里德曼认为的其他两种解释不同，这个解释按时间顺序排列（按年代）。第二次世界大战后，美国的不平等现象随着每周工作时间的延长而减少。但自 20 世纪 70 年代初以来，这一数字急剧上升。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Keynes’s prediction of a shorter working week rests on the idea that the standard of living would continue rising for everyone. But Friedman says that this is not what has happened. Although Keynes’s eight-fold figure holds up for the economy as a whole, it is not at all the case for the median (中位数的) American worker. For them, output by 2029 is likely to be around 3.5 times what it was when Keynes was writing. This is a bit below his four- to eight-fold predicted range.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 凯恩斯对缩短每周工作时间的预测基于这样的想法：每个人的生活水平将继续提高。但弗里德曼表示，事实并非如此。尽管凯恩斯的八倍数字对整个经济来说是成立的，但对美国工人中位数来说却完全不是这样。对他们来说，到 2029 年产出可能是凯恩斯写作时的 3.5 倍左右。这略低于他预测范围的四到八倍。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) This can be seen in the median worker’s income over this time period, complete with a shift in 1973 that fits in precisely with when the working week stopped shrinking. According to Friedman, between 1947 and 1973 the average hourly wage for normal workers (those who were not in management roles) in private industries other than agriculture nearly doubled in terms of what their money could buy. But by 2013 the average hourly wage for ordinary workers had fallen 5 percent from the 1973 level in terms of actual purchasing power. Thus, though American incomes may have gone up since 1973, the amount that American workers can actually buy with their money has gone down. For most Americans, then, the magic of increasing productivity stopped working around 1973. Thus, they had to keep working just as much in order to maintain their standard of living.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 这可以从这一时期工人收入中位数中看出，1973 年的变化恰好与每周工作时间停止缩短的时间相吻合。根据弗里德曼的说法，从 1947 年到 1973 年间，农业以外的私营行业的普通工人（不担任管理职务的工人）的平均时薪就他们的钱能买到的东西而言几乎翻了一番。但到2013年，按实际购买力计算，普通工人的平均小时工资比1973年下降了5%。因此，尽管自 1973 年以来美国人的收入可能有所增加，但美国工人实际能用自己的钱购买的东西却下降了。对于大多数美国人来说，提高生产力的魔力在 1973 年左右就不再起作用了。因此，他们必须继续工作才能维持生活水平。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) What Keynes predicted was a very optimistic version of what economists call technological unemployment. This is the idea that less labor will be necessary because machines can do so much. In Keynes’s vision, the resulting unemployment would be distributed more or less evenly across society in the form of increased leisure. But Friedman says that, for Americans, reality is much darker. Americans now have a labor market in which millions of people — those with fewer skills and less education — are seeking whatever poorly paid work they can get. This is confirmed by a recent poll that found that, for half of hourly workers, their top concern is not that they work too much but that they work too little. This is most likely not because they like their jobs so much. Rather, we can assume it is because they need the money.
paragraphs.translationZh: I）凯恩斯的预测是经济学家所说的技术性失业的非常乐观的版本。这个想法是因为机器可以做很多事情，所以需要更少的劳动力。在凯恩斯的设想中，由此产生的失业将以增加休闲的形式或多或少均匀地分布在整个社会。但弗里德曼表示，对于美国人来说，现实要黑暗得多。美国现在的劳动力市场上有数以百万计的人——那些技能和教育程度较低的人——正在寻找他们能找到的任何低薪工作。最近的一项民意调查证实了这一点，该民意调查发现，对于一半的小时工来说，他们最担心的不是工作太多，而是工作太少。这很可能不是因为他们非常喜欢自己的工作。相反，我们可以假设这是因为他们需要钱。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) This explanation leaves an important question. If the very rich — the workers who have reaped above-average gains from the increased productivity since Keynes’s time — can afford to work less, why do they continue to work so much? (Indeed, research has shown that the highest earners in America tend to work the most.) Friedman believes that for many top earners, work is a labor of love. They are doing work they care about and are interested in, and doing more of it is not necessarily a burden. For them, it may even be a pleasure. These top earners derive meaning from their jobs and work is an important part of how they think of themselves. And, of course, they are compensated for it at a level that makes it worth their while.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 这个解释留下了一个重要的问题。如果非常富有的人——自凯恩斯时代以来从生产率提高中获得高于平均水平的收益的工人——能够负担得起更少的工作，那么为什么他们还要继续工作这么多呢？ （事实上​​，研究表明，美国收入最高的人往往工作得最多。）弗里德曼认为，对于许多收入最高的人来说，工作是一种热爱的劳动。他们在做自己关心、感兴趣的工作，做多了并不一定是一种负担。对于他们来说，这甚至可能是一种乐趣。这些高收入者从他们的工作中获得意义，工作是他们如何看待自己的重要组成部分。当然，他们会得到一定程度的补偿，值得他们付出努力。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Friedman concludes that the prosperity (繁荣) Keynes predicted is here. After all, the economy as a whole has grown even more brilliantly than he expected. But for most Americans, that prosperity is nowhere to be seen. And, as a result, neither are those shorter working weeks.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 弗里德曼得出结论，凯恩斯所预言的繁荣已经到来。毕竟，整个经济的增长比他预想的更加辉煌。但对于大多数美国人来说，这种繁荣却是无处可见的。因此，较短的工作周也不会受到影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Some people view socializing at the workplace as a chance to develop personal relationships.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 有些人将工作场所的社交视为发展人际关系的机会。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. As ordinary American workers’ average hourly pay had decreased despite increasing productivity, they had to work just as many hours as before to keep their living standards.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 尽管生产力提高了，但美国普通工人的平均小时工资却下降了，他们不得不像以前一样工作很多时间来维持生活水平。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. American workers’ average weekly working time has not changed for nearly half a century.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38.美国工人的平均每周工作时间近半个世纪以来没有变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Friedman believes inequality in the U.S. largely explains why increasing productivity has not resulted in reduced working hours.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 弗里德曼认为，美国的不平等在很大程度上解释了为什么生产率的提高并没有导致工作时间的减少。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Many economists assume people’s thirst for material things has prevented them from enjoying more leisure time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 许多经济学家认为人们对物质的渴望阻碍了他们享受更多的闲暇时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. An economist’s prediction about a shorter average working week seemed to be correct for a time in the 20th century.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 一位经济学家关于缩短平均每周工作时间的预测在 20 世纪的一段时间内似乎是正确的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. In the U.S. labor market, the primary concern of people with less schooling and fewer skills is to secure any employment even if it is low-paid.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 在美国劳动力市场，受教育程度较低、技能较少的人最关心的是如何找到工作，即使是低薪的工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Keynes was right in predicting that technology would make the economy much more productive.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 凯恩斯正确地预测，技术将使经济生产力大大提高。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Many of the highest earners have a keen interest in and love for what they are doing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 许多收入最高的人对他们正在做的事情有着浓厚的兴趣和热爱。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. According to Keynes, there would be a shorter working week with everyone’s standard of living continuing to rise.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 根据凯恩斯的观点，随着每个人的生活水平持续提高，每周的工作时间将会缩短。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Lao Zi once said, “Care about what other people think and you will always be their prisoner.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 老子曾经说过：“在意别人的想法，你就永远是他们的囚徒。”

paragraphs.sourceText: People-pleasing, or seeking self-worth through others’ approval, is unproductive and an exhausting way to go through life. Why do we allow what others think of us to have so much power over how we feel about ourselves? If it’s true that you can’t please all people all of the time, wouldn’t it make sense to stop trying?
paragraphs.translationZh: 讨人喜欢，或者通过他人的认可来寻求自我价值，是没有生产力的，也是一种令人筋疲力尽的生活方式。为什么我们允许别人对我们的看法对我们对自己的感受有如此大的影响力？如果你确实无法一直取悦所有人，那么停止尝试不是有意义吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: Unfortunately, sense often isn’t driving our behavior. For social beings who desire love and belonging, wanting to be liked, and caring about the effect we have on others, is healthy and allows us to make connections. However, where we get into trouble is when our self-worth is dependent upon whether we win someone’s approval or not.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不幸的是，感官通常并不能驱动我们的行为。对于那些渴望爱和归属感、希望被人喜欢、关心我们对他人的影响的社会人来说，这是健康的，可以让我们建立联系。然而，当我们的自我价值取决于我们是否赢得某人的认可时，我们就会遇到麻烦。

paragraphs.sourceText: This need to be liked can be traced back to when we were children and were completely dependent on others to take care of us: Small children are not just learning how to walk and communicate, they are also trying to learn how the world works. We learn about who we are and what is expected of us based on interactions with others, so, to a four-year-old, if Mommy or Daddy doesn’t like him or her, there is the danger that they will abandon them. We need to understand that when we desperately want someone to approve of us, it’s being driven by that little kid part of us that is still terrified of abandonment.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种被喜欢的需要可以追溯到我们小时候完全依赖别人照顾我们的时候：小孩子不仅仅是在学习如何走路和交流，他们也在尝试了解世界是如何运作的。我们通过与他人的互动来了解自己是谁以及对我们的期望，因此，对于四岁的孩子来说，如果妈妈或爸爸不喜欢他或她，他们就有抛弃他们的危险。我们需要明白，当我们迫切希望有人认可我们时，我们内心仍然害怕被遗弃的小孩的部分驱使着我们。

paragraphs.sourceText: As you become more capable of providing yourself with the approval you seek, your need for external validation will start to vanish, leaving you stronger, more confident, and yes, happier in your life. Imagine how much time we lose each moment we restrain our authentic selves in an effort to be liked.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当你变得更有能力为自己提供你所寻求的认可时，你对外部认可的需求就会开始消失，让你变得更坚强、更自信，是的，你的生活更快乐。想象一下，我们为了讨人喜欢而克制真实的自我，每一刻我们都浪费了多少时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: If we base our worth on the opinions of others, we cheat ourselves of the power to shape our experiences and embrace life not only for others but also for ourselves, because ultimately, there is no difference. So embrace the cliché (老话) and love yourself as it’s highly doubtful that you’ll regret it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果我们将自己的价值建立在他人的意见之上，那么我们就欺骗了自己，失去了塑造自己经历的能力，也失去了拥抱生活的能力，不仅是为了他人，也是为了自己，因为最终，没有什么区别。因此，拥抱陈词滥调并爱自己，因为你很可能会后悔。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Some people have said aging is more a slide into forgetfulness than a journey towards wisdom. However, a growing body of research suggests that late-in-life learning is possible. In reality, education does an aging brain good.
paragraphs.translationZh: 有人说，衰老与其说是走向智慧的旅程，不如说是陷入健忘的过程。然而，越来越多的研究表明晚年学习是可能的。事实上，教育对老化的大脑有好处。

paragraphs.sourceText: Throughout life, people’s brains constantly renovate themselves. In the late 1960s, British brain scientist Geoffrey Raisman spied growth in damaged brain regions of rats through an electron microscope; their brains were forging new connections. This meant brains may change every time a person learns something new.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在一生中，人们的大脑不断自我更新。 20 世纪 60 年代末，英国脑科学家杰弗里·雷斯曼 (Geoffrey Raisman) 通过电子显微镜观察了老鼠受损大脑区域的生长情况；他们的大脑正在建立新的联系。这意味着每当一个人学习新东西时，大脑可能会发生变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: Of course, that doesn’t mean the brain isn’t affected by the effects of time. Just as height usually declines over the years, so does brain volume: Humans lose about 4 percent every decade starting in their 40s. But that reduction doesn’t necessarily make people think slower; as long as we are alive and functioning, we can alter our brains with new information and experiences.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当然，这并不意味着大脑不受时间的影响。正如身高通常会随着时间的推移而下降一样，大脑容量也会随之下降：从 40 多岁开始，人类每十年就会减少 4% 左右。但这种减少并不一定会让人们思考速度变慢；只要我们还活着并正常运转，我们就可以用新的信息和经验来改变我们的大脑。

paragraphs.sourceText: In fact, scientists now suspect accumulating novel experiences, facts, and skills can keep people’s minds more flexible. New pathways can strengthen our ever-changing mental structure, even as the brain shrinks.
paragraphs.translationZh: 事实上，科学家现在怀疑积累新的经验、事实和技能可以让人们的思维更加灵活。新的途径可以加强我们不断变化的心理结构，即使大脑缩小了。

paragraphs.sourceText: Conventional fixes like word puzzles and brain-training apps can contribute to mental durability. Even something as simple as taking a different route to the grocery store or going somewhere new on vacation can keep the brain healthy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 文字谜题和大脑训练应用程序等传统的修复方法可以有助于提高心理耐久性。即使是像采取不同的路线去杂货店或去新的地方度假这样简单的事情也可以保持大脑健康。

paragraphs.sourceText: A desire for new life challenges can further boost brainpower. Research about aging adults who take on new enterprises shows improved function and memory as well as a reduced risk of mental disease. Openness — a characteristic defined by curiosity and a desire for knowledge — may also help folks pass brain tests. Some folks are born with this take-in-the-world attitude, but those who aren’t as genetically gifted aren’t necessarily out of luck. While genes can encourage an interest in doing new things, a 2012 study in the journal Psychology and Aging found completing reasoning tasks like puzzles and number games can enhance that desire for novel experiences, which can, in turn, refresh the brain. That’s why brain scientist Richard Kennedy says “It’s not that old dogs can’t learn new tricks. It’s that maybe old dogs don’t realize why they should.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 对新生活挑战的渴望可以进一步增强脑力。对从事新事业的老年人的研究表明，老年人的功能和记忆力得到改善，患精神疾病的风险也降低。开放性——一种由好奇心和求知欲望定义的特征——也可能有助于人们通过大脑测试。有些人生来就有这种包容世界的态度，但那些没有如此天赋的人也不一定运气不好。虽然基因可以激发人们对新事物的兴趣，但《心理学与衰老》杂志 2012 年的一项研究发现，完成拼图和数字游戏等推理任务可以增强人们对新奇体验的渴望，从而使大脑焕然一新。这就是为什么大脑科学家理查德·肯尼迪说：“并不是老狗不能学习新技巧。而是也许老狗没有意识到为什么它们应该学习。”

options.sourceText: We should see through other people’s attempt to make a prisoner of us.
options.reflowSourceText: We should see through other people’s attempt to make a prisoner of us.
options.translationZh: 我们应该识破别人企图囚禁我们的企图。

options.sourceText: We can never really please other people even if we try as hard as we can.
options.reflowSourceText: We can never really please other people even if we try as hard as we can.
options.translationZh: 即使我们尽了最大努力，我们也永远无法真正取悦别人。

options.sourceText: We can never be truly free if taking to heart others’ opinion of us.
options.reflowSourceText: We can never be truly free if taking to heart others’ opinion of us.
options.translationZh: 如果把别人对我们的看法放在心上，我们永远不可能真正自由。

options.sourceText: We should care about other people’s view as much as they care about our own.
options.reflowSourceText: We should care about other people’s view as much as they care about our own.
options.translationZh: 我们应该关心别人的观点，就像他们关心我们自己的观点一样。

options.sourceText: Our desire to be loved will be fulfilled.
options.reflowSourceText: Our desire to be loved will be fulfilled.

options.reflowSourceText: Our life will be unfruitful and exhausting.

options.sourceText: Our sense of self will be sharpened and enhanced.

options.sourceText: Our desperate longing for interactions with others.

options.sourceText: Strengthen our power of imagination.
options.reflowSourceText: Strengthen our power of imagination.

options.sourceText: Embrace life for ourselves and for others.
options.reflowSourceText: Embrace life for ourselves and for others.

options.sourceText: Base our worth on others’ opinions.
options.reflowSourceText: Base our worth on others’ opinions.

options.sourceText: See our experiences as assets.
options.reflowSourceText: See our experiences as assets.

options.sourceText: Love ourselves as we are.
options.reflowSourceText: Love ourselves as we are.

options.sourceText: Their wisdom grows as time goes by.
options.reflowSourceText: Their wisdom grows as time goes by.

options.sourceText: Their memory gradually deteriorates.
options.reflowSourceText: Their memory gradually deteriorates.

options.sourceText: They can benefit from late-in-life learning.
options.reflowSourceText: They can benefit from late-in-life learning.

options.sourceText: They are likely to have mental health issues.
options.reflowSourceText: They are likely to have mental health issues.
options.translationZh: 他们很可能有心理健康问题。

options.sourceText: Brain damage seriously hinders one’s learning.
options.reflowSourceText: Brain damage seriously hinders one’s learning.
options.translationZh: 大脑损伤严重阻碍一个人的学习。

options.sourceText: Brain power weakens slower than we imagine.
options.reflowSourceText: Brain power weakens slower than we imagine.
options.translationZh: 脑力减弱的速度比我们想象的要慢。

options.sourceText: Brains can refresh and improve with learning.
options.reflowSourceText: Brains can refresh and improve with learning.

options.sourceText: Brains forge connections under new conditions.
options.reflowSourceText: Brains forge connections under new conditions.

options.sourceText: Doing daily routines by conventional means.
options.reflowSourceText: Doing daily routines by conventional means.

options.sourceText: Avoiding worrying about our mental durability.
options.reflowSourceText: Avoiding worrying about our mental durability.

options.reflowSourceText: Imitating old dogs’ way of learning new tricks.

options.sourceText: Approaching everyday tasks in novel ways.
options.reflowSourceText: Approaching everyday tasks in novel ways.

options.sourceText: Being curious and desiring knowledge.
options.reflowSourceText: Being curious and desiring knowledge.

options.sourceText: Being eager to pass brain tests at an old age.
options.reflowSourceText: Being eager to pass brain tests at an old age.
options.translationZh: 年老时渴望通过大脑测试。

options.sourceText: Rising to life’s challenges and avoiding risks.
options.reflowSourceText: Rising to life’s challenges and avoiding risks.
options.translationZh: 迎接生活挑战并避免风险。

options.sourceText: Boosting immunity to serious mental diseases.
options.reflowSourceText: Boosting immunity to serious mental diseases.

options.sourceText: Wishing to solve puzzles enhances one’s reasoning power.
options.reflowSourceText: Wishing to solve puzzles enhances one’s reasoning power.
options.translationZh: 想要解决难题可以增强一个人的推理能力。

options.sourceText: Playing number games unexpectedly stimulates one’s memory.
options.reflowSourceText: Playing number games unexpectedly stimulates one’s memory.

options.sourceText: Desiring new experiences can help to renovate the brain.
options.reflowSourceText: Desiring new experiences can help to renovate the brain.
